answer: A bond of 44% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Deposits are visible in mesa, and falcon reconciles the forfeits at each close. Because the custody account is separate, a hostile operator cannot recycle one pool of capital across 161 aliases, and each one needs its own funded beacon account. That is 534 dollars of sunk cost for a share worth less than the deposit itself. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
